messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 decode latency spike in us-west-2 (service: inference-api). Threshold breached: p99 > 1.2s for the last 10m. Affected routes: /v1/generate (streaming).
anya (oncall): saw the page, jumping in. is this across all models or specific families?
matt (runtime): early look — mostly Transformer-based models at longer seqs (>1024). p95 up too but p99 is worse. Streaming stalls reported (clients hang mid-stream).
anya (oncall): are we seeing any OOMs or node evictions?
riya (ml-infra): no OOMs in kube events. I see kernel compile jobs churned yesterday for trt-22.1 -> trt-22.2 and a flashattn update landed to runtime-compile branch around 1890001200.
jon (sre): pulling metrics: tail latency correlates with increased kernel compile path times on startup and a spike in GPU context switch duration. attaching traces in a sec.
matt (runtime): interesting — the new flashattn-v2 kernels changed the launch configuration; there's a new fallback in compile path that can cause a slow path for decode when kv-cache allocation crosses a page boundary. Might cause extra GPU memcpy + sync.
anya (oncall): can we confirm with a repro on staging? matt, can you run a short reproduce with long sequence streaming?
matt (runtime): doing a quick run on staging (model: redwood-7b-chi, seq=1536, streaming). log snippet:
```
[decode] kernel_select: using compile-path v3 -> fallback to slow-kernel (flashattn-v2-fallback)
[gpu] memcpy_async wait for event: 12.3ms
[trace] stream_chunk_send: stall detected > 250ms
```
matt (runtime): that matches production pattern.
riya (ml-infra): also noticed we flipped compiler flags for that CI build: `-O3 -ffp-contract=fast -march=native`. Could be exposing numerical assumptions that hit the compile fallback.
anya (oncall): customer impact? brian?
brian (customer-success): I checked support queue — three customers reported truncated streams and one enterprise customer saw 15% error rate for their chat endpoint in us-west-2 over the last 20m. They flagged an SLA alert.
anya (oncall): ok mitigation plan: 1) quickly route streaming traffic away from us-west-2 to us-east-1 for affected customers (soft-failover), 2) pin model runtime to previous kernel variant (rollback flashattn), 3) increase replicas to reduce per-instance queueing. who can action each?
matt (runtime): I can build and push a pinned runtime image with flashattn-v1 kernels (will take ~10-15m).
riya (ml-infra): I can start route steering for a subset of customers via routing table change and bump replicas for the inference pool. Need list of route keys to shift.
jon (sre): I'll open an incident page and run a quick autoscaler override to add 30% capacity to the pool. Also enabling debug-level GPU kernel traces for the affected hosts.
anya (oncall): matt, please include a note in the image tag `rollback/flashattn-v1-189000`. deploy-bot, can we do a canary rollout immediately after image is available?
deploy-bot: Received deployment request. Canary strategy: 5% -> 20% after 5m -> 50% after 10m if no errors. Approving automated rollout.
matt (runtime): image built and pushed: `registry.redwood/inference/runtime:rollback-flashattn-v1-189000`. Starting canary now.
anya (oncall): riya, start routing for the flagged enterprise customer to us-east-1 only. keep other customers on multi-region unless errors continue.
riya (ml-infra): routing rule applied for customer-id C-9812 and C-7741. Confirmed traffic shift ~2 minutes ago.
jon (sre): autoscale override applied, additional nodes provisioning. early signs: p95 trending down, p99 still elevated but improving.
matt (runtime): canary shows significantly fewer fallback kernel selects. logs now: `kernel_select: using flashattn-v1 fast-path` and stream chunk latency < 40ms typical.
brian (customer-success): customers on the routing change report improved streaming behavior. enterprise C-9812 acknowledges reduced errors.
anya (oncall): good. next steps: keep rollback runtime in place for us-west-2 while we debug root cause. matt/riya, can we capture a minimal reproducer that isolates compile-time selection criteria (seq length, kv alignment, compiler flags)?
matt (runtime): I'll instrument a variant that logs `kv_alloc_alignment`, `kernel_choice`, and `gpu_sync_time` for reproducer runs. aiming for a full artifact in ~2h.
riya (ml-infra): I'll re-run CI build with old compiler flags `-O2 -fno-fast-math` and compare resulting kernel binary sizes & symbol diffs. might reveal why fallback triggers.
jon (sre): we'll keep debug traces for 3 hours then scale back. also flagging infrastructure backlog to add guards so compile-path falling back doesn't block streaming (async compile + serve with older kernel).
anya (oncall): handoff for next oncall (matt will be primary owner for root cause). jon you're SRE escalation contact. riya owns CI/flag comparison. I'll remain in loop for customer comms.
matt (runtime): Handoff note: current state — rollback image deployed to canary and ramped to 50% in us-west-2, routing for impacted customers to us-east-1, autoscale override in effect. Collecting reproducer and kernel traces.
jon (sre): Handoff note: infra checks healthy, nodes continue to provision. retention of debug traces enabled. contact me if p99 rises above 1.0s again.
anya (oncall): Brian, please update C-9812 with mitigation summary and ETA for full fix (we expect a patch/PR within 48h after reproducer).
brian (customer-success): will ping them now and share the rollback + routing mitigation. includes promise to follow up with root cause once triage completes.
matt (runtime): one more data point — the fallback path seems triggered when `kv_size % 4096 != 0` combined with compilers producing different vectorized loops. if that holds we'll have a clear hypothesis.
riya (ml-infra): got it. I'll try replicate with forced misaligned KV allocations.
anya (oncall): thanks everyone. set reminder: incident-check-in in 45m. if anyone finds immediate regressions, post here. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #INC-189000-DecodeTail-FlashFallback. Severity: sev2. Paging policy applied.
anya (oncall): closing the oncall thread — handoff completed. keeping channel open for updates.
jon (sre): :eyes: updating incident doc with links to traces and the rollback image.
